content.user_title: Build Azure Queue Workflows in Python
content.value_statement: Developers often need reliable queue examples without searching Azure SDK docs. This skill gives focused Python snippets for sending, receiving, updating, and managing Azure Queue Storage messages.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install Azure Queue Storage and Azure Identity packages.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential authentication for QueueServiceClient and QueueClient.
Provides examples for creating, listing, and deleting queues.
Explains sending, receiving, peeking, updating, and deleting queue messages.
Includes async client usage for higher throughput queue processing.
Covers Base64 policies for binary queue message content.
limitations: Does not provision Azure resources or create storage accounts.
Does not validate credentials, permissions, or network access in your environment.
Does not replace production testing for retry, poison message, or error handling behavior.
Does not cover advanced Service Bus features such as topics or sessions.

use_cases.title: Add Queue Messaging to an App
use_cases.description: Use Python examples to send work items to Azure Queue Storage and process them later.

use_cases.title: Build Background Workers
use_cases.description: Create worker logic that receives messages, extends visibility, and deletes completed work safely.

use_cases.title: Review Queue Operations
use_cases.description: Compare common queue operations before writing runbooks, tests, or internal implementation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Queue Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show the basic Python setup for Azure Queue Storage with DefaultAzureCredential. Include the required packages and client setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Send and Receive Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a Python workflow that sends a message, receives messages, prints useful metadata, and deletes each processed message.

prompt_templates.title: Design Worker Visibility Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a worker pattern that handles visibility timeout, dequeue count, retries, and safe deletion after successful processing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Async Queue Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an async Python queue processor for Azure Queue Storage. Include client lifecycle, message handling, and operational safeguards.

output_examples.input: Explain how to receive messages and avoid duplicate processing.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow describing visibility timeout, processing steps, deletion after success, and retry behavior for failed messages.

output_examples.input: Summarize queue operations for a new backend developer.
output: Create or select a queue before sending messages.
Use receive operations to hide messages during processing.
Delete messages only after successful work completion.

output_examples.input: Help me decide when to use the async client.
output_examples.output: Guidance that compares synchronous and async clients for throughput, concurrency, worker scale, and application complexity.

best_practices: Use managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential instead of embedding secrets in code.
Set visibility timeout and time to live values based on real processing behavior.
Track dequeue count and route repeated failures to a poison message process.
anti_patterns: Do not delete messages before processing is complete.
Do not hardcode storage account secrets, connection strings, or real account URLs in shared prompts.
Do not use Queue Storage when you need topics, sessions, or complex broker features.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you write Python workflows for Azure Queue Storage messaging, worker processing, and queue management.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK examples and guidance, but you must create and configure Azure resources separately.

faq.question: Which authentication method does it show?
faq.answer: It shows DefaultAzureCredential, which supports managed identity, developer login, and other Azure Identity flows.

faq.question: Can it handle binary messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Base64 encode and decode policy examples for binary queue message content.

faq.question: Does it include async examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an async QueueClient pattern for sending, receiving, and deleting messages.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for production review?
faq.answer: No. You still need environment testing, error handling review, retry design, and access control validation.
